title: Wyndham Street North redesign approved
subtitle: Also: parking payment-in-lieu policy, new joint social services and ambulance committee with county, integrity commissioner report.
overview: Council directed staff to rebuild Wyndham Street North between Carden and Woolwich streets with one traffic lane each way, parallel parking and separated bike paths on both sides. St. George's Square will stay an offset intersection with operational improvements {{vote:m10}}. A transit user raised concerns about buses. Staff said transit stops would be kept and transit needs would be handled in detailed design.

Council also approved a Payment-in-lieu of Off-street Parking Policy, effective March 1, 2024 {{vote:m9}}. It lets developers pay a fee instead of providing some parking. Council endorsed terms of reference for a new joint committee with Wellington County on social services and land ambulance, and appointed its city members {{vote:m12}}. Councillor Busuttil was appointed as the city's chair or vice-chair representative {{vote:m14}}.

The consent report passed, including a transfer of the one-time physician recruitment contribution to the Guelph-Wellington Ontario Health Team. Two people were appointed to the Committee of Adjustment. After the closed session, the mayor said staff were given direction on a bargaining mandate and on an Ontario Land Tribunal matter.

decisions.detail: Staff were directed to rebuild the corridor from Carden to Woolwich streets with one lane each way, parallel parking, separated bike paths and flexibility for seasonal patios, and to keep St. George's Square as an offset intersection.
Council approved the policy effective March 1, 2024 and amended the development application fee by-law to add the estimated cost of a parking space and the application fee.

decisions.item: Joint social services and ambulance committee
decisions.detail: Council endorsed the terms of reference for a joint committee with Wellington County on social services and land ambulance.
The Mayor, the chairs of Public Services and Infrastructure and of Development and Environment, and the vice-chair of Governance were appointed to the joint committee.
Councillor Busuttil was appointed as the city's chair or vice-chair representative on the joint committee for a term ending November 30, 2024.

The one-time budgeted contribution for physician recruitment will go to the Guelph-Wellington Ontario Health Team even though the Guelph Chamber of Commerce's matching contribution has not been received.
Nicole Segal and Pamela Membreno were appointed to the Committee of Adjustment for a term ending in November 2026.

debate: On parking, one councillor opposed the policy because money collected from developers who provide less parking should go only to future infrastructure, or the downtown should have no minimum parking requirements so units get built faster.
The mayor also voted against the parking policy, saying that it was hard to support a policy built on parking minimums the mayor fundamentally disagrees with in the downtown.

A transit-user delegate said the Wyndham plan barely mentioned transit and doubted two lanes could keep traffic moving with on-street parking. The delegate worried buses would be delayed behind parking cars and that transit access at St. George's Square could be lost.

Staff said transit staff were involved in the design, that existing bus stops would stay with no parking where buses stop, and that details would be settled in detailed design. Councillors asked about transit laybys, delivery vehicles and later public input. Staff pointed to open houses and review at about 60 or 90 percent design.

On the joint committee, councillors asked why committee chairs were chosen rather than the usual appointment process. Staff said it was a proposed starting point that council could change. Staff also said final ambulance budget and operational decisions would stay with city council, and fire services would not be part of the committee.
